## Natural history notes

A small orange-and-black butterfly characterized by orange wings with dark checkered markings, pale crescent-shaped spots, and a thin, dark, strongly patterned underside. In Florida, it is found in sunny open habitats such as roadsides, fields, prairies, lawns, gardens, pine flatwoods, and disturbed areas where low flowering plants are common. Adults feed on nectar from small wildflowers, while the caterpillars feed mainly on frogfruit and related plants, often using low groundcover vegetation as both food and shelter.
